newsitem.title: JAPAN: Asian bourses close out strong week on a high note.
newsitem.headline: Asian bourses close out strong week on a high note.

text.p: Wall Street's winning ways rubbed off on Tokyo and Hong Kong on Friday while stock markets elsewhere in Asia also capped a strong week with solid gains.

Tokyo stocks took heart from the Dow Jones Industrial Index's record close overnight and from hopes that Sunday's parliamentary elections may return a government stable enough to do something to help the economy.
The key Nikkei 225 index ended 188.56 points, or 0.88 percent, higher at 21,612.30.
Market sources said activity was fuelled by media polls showing that the Liberal Democratic Party may win a clear majority of seats in Japan's election.
"Institutional investors were buying in anticipation of the elections," said Daiichi Securities analyst Akishige Ishikura. "Futures-linked trade also made the market hum with activity."

In Hong Kong, the Hang Seng Index advanced 73.25 points, or 0.59 percent, to close at a record high of 12,510.05. The market was buoyed by institutional and retail buyers emboldened by New York, brokers said.
"We saw some intra-day profit-taking, then the market regained confidence to follow Wall Street's lead and move ahead," said one broker with a UK-based house.
The main Philippine index sustained its two-day surge on strong buying in most front- and second-liners, traders said.
"It looks like it's the start of recovery. We are seeing a lot of funds come in," said Russel Ong, analyst at Anscor-Hagedorn Securities Inc.
The index soared 38.67 points, 1.26 percent, to 3,099.73 points.
Thai stocks saw their third straight day of gains, advancing 1.99 percent in moderate trade after investors bought blue-chip stocks in key sectors, brokers said.
The SET index finished 18.48 points up at 948.09 on 5.4 billion baht turnover.
Foreign institutional buyers propelled Malaysia's stock market, snapping up blue-chip stocks in large volumes, equities dealers and analysts said.
The Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised stocks closed 17.18 points, or 1.48 percent, higher at 1175.60.
Australian shares ended a touch firmer with profit-taking dragging the market off its early highs as investors decided to square positions following record highs during the week.
The benchmark All Ordinaries index closed just 1.2 points higher at 2,355.0, up 0.05 percent but well off its intra-day high of 2,369.3.
Stocks in Seoul, Singapore and Taipei provided the only sour notes for the region.
South Korea's composite stock index fell on profit-taking in small and mid-cap shares, brokers said. The index fell 9.48 points, or 1.13 percent, to close provisionally at 830.25.
Singapore stocks slipped in listless trade, with the Straits Times Industrial Index closing down 4.2 points, or 0.20 percent, at 2,064.52 points.
Taipei's index fell slightly in thin trading, ending down 0.29 percent, or 18.92 points, at 6,475.42
At 1130 GMT, the dollar was trading at 112.42/2.52 yen and 1.5423/26 marks.

SIMEX Brent December futures were indicated slightly firmer in late afternoon trading, supported by political changes in Russia and stock figures showing a draw in distillates in the United States. December was quoted at $24.24/$24.30 per barrel, up from London's Thursday close of $24.19.
Gold prices eased in Hong Kong but ended up from the day's low on late selling Friday, dealers said. Bullion closed at US$379.60/380.10, down from New York's Thursday close of US$380.40/90.
